<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Pass allocator-produced axis semantics alongside KV tensors at connector registration. This distinguishes `[B, 2, H, 1, N, D]` from `[2, B, H, 1, N, D]` even when `B == 2` and shape and strides are identical.

Related: #42082, [RBLN producer PoC](https://github.com/RBLN-SW/vllm-rbln/pull/1297), [LMCache#5866](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/5866).

## Illustrated review guide

[**Read the blog article (English)**](https://maobaolong.github.io/en/blog/vllm-kv-cache-axis-registration/) · [**中文**](https://maobaolong.github.io/blog/vllm-kv-cache-axis-registration/) · [Standalone English snapshot](https://github.com/maobaolong/vllm/blob/ed5f19fe535c5f3d75ae6e038d6caba931ca3ee7/index.html)

The complete English and Chinese versions share the blog's language-switch button and saved preference. 15 diagrams and two interactive examples explain the motivation, exact allocation-to-connector call chains, axis semantics versus physical strides and content encoding, RBLN/MLA/hybrid views, compatibility, related work, and the remaining LMCache consumer/MP integration. Code links pin the reviewed `3838746` snapshot; the guide is a native blog article, separate from this PR's code diff.

<details>
<summary>Preview: the two-block ambiguity and metadata propagation</summary>

[![Same shape and strides, different K/V sequences](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maobaolong/vllm/ed5f19fe535c5f3d75ae6e038d6caba931ca3ee7/assets/axis-ambiguity.png)](https://maobaolong.github.io/en/blog/vllm-kv-cache-axis-registration/#ambiguity)

[![Metadata from view creation through model runner to connector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maobaolong/vllm/ed5f19fe535c5f3d75ae6e038d6caba931ca3ee7/assets/registration-call-chain.png)](https://maobaolong.github.io/en/blog/vllm-kv-cache-axis-registration/#mrv2)

</details>

## Claims

- `create_kv_cache_views` declares `[BLOCK, HEAD, STATE, CONTENT]` when it creates each standard view. Both GPU model runners forward those declarations, including shared-layer aliases; HiSparse host views use the same view creator. Raw storage remains unspecified.
- `MultiConnector` forwards descriptors to each child. Existing connectors inherit a default that validates metadata and calls their tensor-only registration hook.
- Custom allocators can declare separate KV and singleton axes. Actual tensor shape, strides, dtype and storage offset remain authoritative for addressing; axis roles do not imply identical hybrid-cache formats.

## Validation

Tested [commit `9be42ea`](https://github.com/maobaolong/vllm/commit/9be42ea8ac8b08019ce921aed003ba3a33a0b65c) on macOS arm64, Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.14.1, against main `4b1c04e76fe9ac3ca8b7e541dd423e7d5f38dc60`. Run from that checkout in a [vLLM development environment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4b1c04e76fe9ac3ca8b7e541dd423e7d5f38dc60/docs/contributing/README.md#developing), with pytest and tblib installed. Existing MultiConnector tests require the cached `facebook/opt-125m` configuration; the planning suite requires `Qwen/Qwen1.5-7B/config.json` cached via `huggingface_hub.hf_hub_download`. No model weights are needed for these CPU suites.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 uv run --no-sync .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_cache_registration.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_kv_connector.py \
  -k 'not multi_example_connector_consistency' -q -rs
# 132 passed, 1 skipped, 1 deselected

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 uv run --no-sync .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_kv_cache_allocation_scope.py -q -rs
# 94 passed
```

The existing GPU LLM test skipped on CPU; `test_multi_example_connector_consistency` was excluded because this host has no GPU/native extension. No serving, hardware-plugin or LMCache consumer/MP E2E result is claimed. The planning suite initially had two configuration-loading failures offline; after caching the Qwen configuration, the full suite passed without test exclusions.

The registration tests use real allocator views and real mixed old/new connectors. They check canonical K/V values at `B == 2`, re-registration, all six stride layouts, padded pages, shared-layer aliases, invalid metadata, and mixed full/sliding-attention and Mamba views with different shapes and dtypes. The existing HiSparse allocation test also verifies host-view metadata and raw-storage omission. New registration cases run in the existing CPU connector CI step. Applicable pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff, mypy and test tethering.

The documentation-only follow-up [`3838746`](https://github.com/maobaolong/vllm/commit/383874621325a7057190711527ad268c183e0b19) clarifies MLA views without a K/V selector. All three documented MLA axis/shape examples were checked with the real `validate_shape`; a size-one `KV` axis was confirmed to raise `ValueError`. Applicable pre-commit hooks passed. Runtime code is unchanged from the tested commit above.

## Details

Axis declarations are generated alongside actual view creation, rather than inferred later by `KVCacheConfig`. Allocators accept an optional fresh `tensor_layouts` output dictionary, preserving existing return types and tensor-only callers. Both runners propagate it to registration and copy descriptors for shared views.

This complements #42082: `KVCacheLayout` describes physical stride order, while the descriptor describes the registered view before attention-private kernel-block mappings. `STATE` follows the cache spec's token granularity; `CONTENT` stays opaque. Packing, encoding, tuple/multi-plane descriptors and external transport schemas remain follow-up work. MRV1 uses the same compatibility hook so existing deployments receive the same contract as MRV2.

RBLN is a concrete downstream user of this API: [vllm-rbln#1297](https://github.com/RBLN-SW/vllm-rbln/pull/1297) declares axes where its custom attention cache shape is chosen, then passes them with the registered per-layer tensors through `register_kv_caches_with_layouts`. Its `[B, 2, H, 1, N, D]` view declares `(BLOCK, KV, HEAD, SINGLETON, STATE, HEAD_DIM)`; the `[2, B, H, 1, N, D]` view swaps the first two roles. RBLN does not need to use the standard BHNC allocator to use this registration hook. The downstream draft depends on this upstream API merging and becoming available in its supported vLLM dependency; it is not a prerequisite for this PR. RBLN hardware validation and the LMCache consumer remain downstream work.

Duplicate checks found no existing registration-axis API. #42374 standardizes allocation; #62107 changes FlashInfer's physical K/V placement. Neither carries these per-view axis declarations to connectors.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, review and validation. Submitted as a draft for API discussion and human review.

- [x] **Testing and Validation:** CPU behavior and allocation suites passed; GPU and external-consumer limits are documented above.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Applicable pre-commit checks passed; the API contract and examples are documented under Design Documents.

</details>

detail.title: [Feature][KV Connector] Pass typed cache axes at registration

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
+# KV cache axis metadata at connector registration
+
+KV connectors can override `register_kv_caches_with_layouts(kv_caches, layouts)`
+to receive producer-declared axis semantics alongside the actual tensors.
+The default implementation validates supplied layouts and delegates to the
+existing `register_kv_caches(kv_caches)` hook. Existing connectors do not need
+to change their method signatures. `MultiConnector` forwards the descriptors
+to each child.
+
+## Descriptor contract
+
+`KVCacheTensorLayout.axes` is a tuple of `KVCacheAxis` enum members in **tensor
+indexing order**. `KVCacheLayout` continues to
+describe the allocator's physical stride permutation. Consumers must use the
+actual tensor's shape, strides, dtype, and storage offset for addressing.
+
+Both GPU model runners pass descriptors produced when the allocator creates
+logical `[block, head, token/state, content]` views, including views with
+padded blocks or layers sharing an allocation. To collect them, pass a fresh
+`tensor_layouts` dictionary to `allocate_kv_cache`; the allocator populates it
+through `create_kv_cache_views`, alongside the returned tensors. Existing
+callers can omit this keyword and keep the tensor-only return value.
+HiSparse collects host-view descriptors through the same view creator.
+Shared layers inherit their target view's descriptor.
+
+Hybrid groups may have different shapes, dtypes, state granularity and content
+encodings while sharing these axis roles. Layer names identify per-layer views;
+the actual tensor's strides and storage offset describe cross-layer packing.
+Descriptors describe the views registered with the connector, before any
+mapping to attention-private kernel-block views. `CONTENT` is opaque: the
+layer's `KVCacheSpec` describes its encoding and packing. Axis metadata alone
+does not identify quantization scales or split packed K and V.
+
+`STATE` counts positions in the view. The cache spec supplies their token
+granularity for compressed or recurrent caches. An explicit `KV` axis has
+size two, with K at index zero and V at index one. `SINGLETON` axes have size
+one and may occur more than once.
+
+The mapping uses the same layer names as `kv_caches`. A missing entry means
+unspecified semantics, not a default layout. Raw storage without semantic
+layer views is omitted. A connector that requires explicit semantics must
+reject such entries or use its existing spec-aware registration path.
+
+### MLA views without a K/V selector
+
+`KV` specifically selects between separately stored K and V; it is not a count
+of cache tensors or latent vectors. MLA stores a shared latent representation
+without a separate V allocation, so its descriptor does not need a `KV` axis.
+For example, a standard MLA view with shape `[blocks, 1, states, content]`
+still declares `(BLOCK, HEAD, STATE, CONTENT)`: the size-one dimension is a
+head slot. The spec defines the latent content's encoding.
+
+Custom MLA views must describe their own indexing order. A
+`[blocks, states, content]` view declares `(BLOCK, STATE, CONTENT)`; a view
+with an extra placeholder dimension `[1, blocks, states, content]` declares
+`(SINGLETON, BLOCK, STATE, CONTENT)`. A size-one dimension that has a semantic
+role, such as `HEAD`, keeps that role rather than becoming `SINGLETON`.
+
+`validate_shape` accepts these views without a `KV` axis. Declaring a size-one
+axis as `KV` is rejected: it would not say whether the entry represents K, V
+or a shared latent. Component roles and content encoding require spec-aware
+handling rather than relaxing the two-element `KV` contract.
+
+## Custom allocators
+
+An out-of-tree backend or model runner should construct descriptors where it
+chooses the registered tensor's layout. It must describe the exact view
+passed to the connector, rather than a later backend-private view.
+
+For example, two RBLN-style layouts can have the identical shape
+`[2, 2, heads, 1, tokens, head_dim]`. Shape or contiguous strides cannot
+distinguish their block and K/V axes. Their declarations are different:
+
+```python
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_layout import KVCacheAxis as Axis
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_layout import KVCacheTensorLayout
+
+tail = (Axis.HEAD, Axis.SINGLETON, Axis.STATE, Axis.HEAD_DIM)
+blocks_first = KVCacheTensorLayout((Axis.BLOCK, Axis.KV, *tail))
+kv_first = KVCacheTensorLayout((Axis.KV, Axis.BLOCK, *tail))
+
+connector.register_kv_caches_with_layouts(
+    {"layer": cache}, {"layer": blocks_first}
+)
+```
+
+The consumer can call `layout.axis_index(Axis.BLOCK)` to locate the block
+dimension and `layout.validate_shape(cache.shape)` to check the rank and
+fixed-size axes. Overriding connectors should validate descriptors before
+using them and reject inconsistent metadata rather than guess a different
+layout. They can map the descriptor to an internal transfer format once
+at registration, without importing a cache library's format enum into vLLM.
+
+Any connector-side permutation, squeeze, reshape or component split must
+transform the descriptor along with its tensor. After a cache reallocation,
+the producer must register the new views with matching descriptors again.
+
+This hook does not itself update external connectors or hardware plugins.
+They must opt in to produce and consume the metadata. The descriptor is an
+in-process Python API; an external connector owns its transport schema.
+Tuple and multi-plane registrations need a matching component description
+in a future extension. An axis declaration alone does not describe their
+component roles or encoding.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+from collections.abc import Mapping
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config import DeviceConfig, KVTransferConfig, SchedulerConfig, VllmConfig
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.base import KVConnectorRole
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.example_connector import (
+    ExampleConnector,
+)
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.multi_connector import MultiConnector
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (
+    FullAttentionSpec,
+    HiSparseResidentSpec,
+    KVCacheConfig,
+    KVCacheGroupSpec,
+    KVCacheTensor,
+    MambaSpec,
+    SlidingWindowSpec,
+    UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs,
+    compute_layout_strides,
+)
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_layout import KVCacheAxis as Axis
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_layout import KVCacheLayout, KVCacheTensorLayout
+from vllm.v1.worker.utils import (
+    add_kv_sharing_layers_to_kv_cache_groups,
+    allocate_kv_cache,
+)
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test
+
+
+class TensorRegistrationConnector(ExampleConnector):
+    def register_kv_caches(self, kv_caches: dict[str, torch.Tensor]):
+        self.registered_caches = kv_caches
+
+
+class AxisRegistrationConnector(TensorRegistrationConnector):
+    def register_kv_caches_with_layouts(
+        self,
+        kv_caches: dict[str, torch.Tensor],
+        layouts: Mapping[str, KVCacheTensorLayout],
+    ) -> None:
+        super().register_kv_caches_with_layouts(kv_caches, layouts)
+        self.layouts = layouts
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def make_connector():
+    def make(kv_cache_config: KVCacheConfig) -> MultiConnector:
+        config = VllmConfig(
+            device_config=DeviceConfig(device="cpu"),
+            scheduler_config=SchedulerConfig(
+                max_model_len=16,
+                max_num_batched_tokens=16,
+                max_num_seqs=1,
+                is_encoder_decoder=False,
+                disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager=True,
+            ),
+            kv_transfer_config=KVTransferConfig(
+                kv_connector="MultiConnector",
+                kv_role="kv_both",
+                kv_connector_extra_config={
+                    "connectors": [
+                        {
+                            "kv_connector": cls.__name__,

This looks like a default for all backends, but some backends change what dim 1 means through customize_spec. For example, `rocm_attn` sets `num_head_slots=2`, so dim 1 is K/V rather than heads, yet it's still labeled HEAD. Wouldn't the connector then get a wrong layout?

Could each backend declare its own layout (e.g. `get_kv_cache_tensor_layout(spec)`), and leave it unset when num_head_slots is set but nothing is declared?
